name: Grok 4.7
description: Grok 4.7 is SpaceXAI's frontier model for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work. It uses a larger base model than Grok 4.6, with longer RL on harder multi-hour tasks, stronger self-verification, and native Grok Bot harness understanding. Reasoning efforts: low, medium, high, xhigh (default high). 500K context; same price and speed class as Grok 4.6 ($2/$0.50 cached/$6 per 1M tokens under 200k prompts; ≥200k prompts bill at $4/$1/$12). Grok 4.7 Fast uses the same model on faster infrastructure at twice the token rates and twice the output speed, and is available only in Cursor and Grok Build — not as a separate public API model id (docs expose only `grok-4.7`). Pretraining knowledge cutoff June 2026, with supplemental training data through August 2026. Multimodal: text and image in, text out.

benchmarks.name: AA-Briefcase v1.1
benchmarks.description: AA-Briefcase v1.1 evaluates multi-hour professional office work and reports Elo scores. Kept separate from unversioned AA-Briefcase results.
benchmarks.analysis_method: AA Briefcase v1.1 Elo; Grok 4.7 xhigh (1657; max_score 3000). Aligned to aa-briefcase-1.1. Sources: announcement + model card PDF.

benchmarks.name: BixBench MCQ
benchmarks.description: BixBench zero-shot multiple-choice accuracy on bioinformatics questions. Kept separate from the agentic BixBench workflow evaluation that requires code execution.
benchmarks.analysis_method: BixBench zero-shot MCQ accuracy; Grok 4.7 high (88.4%). Distinct from agentic BixBench. Sources: model card PDF.

benchmarks.name: CADGenBench
benchmarks.description: CADGenBench evaluates agents on CAD model construction from design prompts. The generation split requires producing CAD geometry graded for executability and geometric correctness. Distinct from BenchCAD.
benchmarks.analysis_method: CADGenBench generation split; Grok 4.7 high (44.4%) with Grok Build harness. Not BenchCAD. Sources: model card PDF.

benchmarks.name: CathedralBench
benchmarks.description: CathedralBench is a third-party red-team cyber evaluation on highly difficult, multiple-exploit-chain tasks in egress-secure sandboxes. Accuracy is commonly reported on the hard subset of tasks in an unrestricted configuration.
benchmarks.analysis_method: CathedralBench hard-subset accuracy; Grok 4.7 xhigh (29%). Unrestricted third-party red-team cyber eval. Sources: model card PDF.

benchmarks.name: CursorBench 4.0
benchmarks.description: CursorBench 4.0 evaluates coding agents on long-horizon coding tasks from real Cursor sessions. Version 4.0 adds longer-horizon tasks; scores are not comparable with CursorBench 3.2.
benchmarks.analysis_method: CursorBench 4.0; Grok 4.7 xhigh (46.3%). Model card also reports 43.9% at high. Scores not comparable to CursorBench 3.2. Sources: announcement + model card PDF.

benchmarks.name: CVE-Bench
benchmarks.description: CVE-Bench evaluates agents on exploiting real-world web-application CVEs in sandboxed environments that mimic production services, typically in unrestricted / egress-controlled settings as a cyber capability probe.
benchmarks.analysis_method: CVE-Bench Reward; Grok 4.7 xhigh primary (36.6%); model card also reports 37.7% at high — not blended. Grok Build harness, unrestricted. Sources: model card PDF.

benchmarks.name: CyberGym
benchmarks.description: CyberGym is a benchmark for evaluating AI agents on cybersecurity tasks, testing their ability to identify vulnerabilities, perform security analysis, and complete security-related challenges in a controlled environment.
benchmarks.analysis_method: CyberGym Mean Reproduced %; Grok 4.7 high (80.3%), unrestricted / without standard safeguards; Grok Build harness. Sources: model card PDF.

benchmarks.name: DeepSWE 1.1
benchmarks.description: DeepSWE 1.1 evaluates software engineering agents using the mini-swe-agent harness.
benchmarks.analysis_method: DeepSWE v1.1; Grok 4.7 high (71.0%; launch comparison table marks high effort with asterisk). Sources: announcement + model card PDF.

benchmarks.name: EEBench
benchmarks.description: EEBench is an electrical engineering and chip design benchmark: models design circuits and other hardware that are graded for physical correctness and functionality.
benchmarks.analysis_method: EEBench; Grok 4.7 xhigh (66.0% from model card, Grok Build harness). News comparison table lists 64.0%; catalog stores the model-card figure, not a blend. Sources: model card PDF + announcement.

benchmarks.name: FrontierSWE V2
benchmarks.description: FrontierSWE V2 evaluates agents on open-ended technical projects and reports mean@5. Kept separate from FrontierSWE V1 dominance-score results, which are not comparable.
benchmarks.analysis_method: FrontierSWE V2 mean@5 (29.0%) at xhigh; Proximal Labs / Proximus harness. Not comparable to V1 dominance scores. Sources: model card PDF.

benchmarks.name: GDPval (Elo)
benchmarks.description: GDPval professional knowledge-work results reported as Elo in xAI's Grok 4.7 announcement. The source does not identify this as GDPval-AA v2; kept separate from that evaluation and percentage-based GDPval scores.
benchmarks.analysis_method: GDPval Elo; Grok 4.7 xhigh 1695 (max_score 3000). Aligned to gdpval-elo. Sources: announcement + model card PDF.

benchmarks.name: Harvey LAB (Vals)
benchmarks.description: Harvey LAB (Vals) is a professional legal-work evaluation of AI systems on complex law-firm style tasks, reported by Vals.
benchmarks.analysis_method: Harvey LAB (Vals); Grok 4.7 xhigh (19.6%). Same id family as Grok 4.6. Sources: announcement + model card PDF.

benchmarks.name: Harvey's Legal Agent Benchmark
benchmarks.description: Harvey's Legal Agent Benchmark evaluates AI agents on complex legal workflows and reports the all-pass rate.
benchmarks.analysis_method: Harvey's Legal Agent Benchmark; Grok 4.7 xhigh. Score reported by xAI.

benchmarks.name: HealthBench Professional
benchmarks.description: HealthBench Professional evaluates model capability and safety for clinician use cases using real clinician-style chats and physician-authored grading rubrics.
benchmarks.analysis_method: HealthBench Professional; Grok 4.7 xhigh (56.7%). Sources: announcement + model card PDF.

benchmarks.name: LAB-Bench Practical
benchmarks.description: LAB-Bench practical is a public multiple-choice evaluation of everyday wet-lab and research skills, covering protocol troubleshooting, sequence reasoning, and cloning scenarios. Distinct from labbench2.
benchmarks.analysis_method: LAB-Bench practical MCQ accuracy; Grok 4.7 high (76.8%). Distinct from labbench2. Sources: model card PDF.

benchmarks.name: LatchBio Capabilities v1.0
benchmarks.description: LatchBio Capabilities v1.0 is a cross-benchmark evaluation of agentic biological data analysis. The overall score is the equally weighted mean of observed scores across 11 capability benchmarks.
benchmarks.analysis_method: LatchBio Capabilities v1.0 overall; Grok 4.7 xhigh (44.5%), equal-weight mean of 11 capability benches. Sources: model card PDF.

benchmarks.name: ProtocolQA Open-Ended
benchmarks.description: ProtocolQA Open-Ended evaluates free-form answers on troubleshooting failed experimental outcomes from common biological laboratory protocols. Kept separate from the multiple-choice ProtocolQA split.
benchmarks.analysis_method: ProtocolQA Open-Ended accuracy; Grok 4.7 high (70.4%). Distinct from MCQ ProtocolQA. Sources: model card PDF.

benchmarks.name: SWE-Marathon
benchmarks.description: SWE-Marathon is an ultra-long-horizon software engineering benchmark covering tasks such as building compilers, optimizing kernels, and developing production-grade services. It measures whether agents can sustain quality across extremely long engineering trajectories.
benchmarks.analysis_method: SWE-Marathon v1.1; Grok 4.7 high (46.0%). Sources: model card PDF.

benchmarks.name: Terminal-Bench 4.0
benchmarks.description: Terminal-Bench 4.0 evaluates AI agents on real-world work in terminal and command-line containerized environments across 66 tasks, with emphasis on science-adjacent and frontier engineering problems. Relative to earlier Terminal-Bench releases, 4.0 increases timeouts and adaptively raises RAM/CPU on selected tasks to reduce harness and resource confounds.
benchmarks.analysis_method: Terminal-Bench 4.0; Grok 4.7 xhigh (38.0%) with Grok Build harness. Sources: announcement + model card PDF.

benchmarks.name: Virology Capabilities Test
benchmarks.description: Virology Capabilities Test (VCT) is an expert-level multiple-choice benchmark measuring the capability to troubleshoot complex virology laboratory protocols. It evaluates dual-use biological knowledge relevant to bioweapons development.
benchmarks.analysis_method: Virology Capabilities Test (VCT) accuracy; Grok 4.7 high (63.0%). Capability signal, not refusal. Sources: model card PDF.

benchmarks.name: WMDP-Bio
benchmarks.description: Biology subset of WMDP (Weapons of Mass Destruction Proxy). Multiple-choice questions measuring dual-use biology knowledge relevant to enabling malicious actors to design, synthesize, acquire, or use biological weapons.
benchmarks.analysis_method: WMDP-Bio accuracy; Grok 4.7 high (88.1%). Dual-use biology MCQ capability signal. Sources: model card PDF.

benchmarks.name: WMDP-Chem
benchmarks.description: Chemistry subset of WMDP (Weapons of Mass Destruction Proxy). Multiple-choice questions measuring dual-use chemistry knowledge relevant to enabling malicious actors to design, synthesize, acquire, or use chemical weapons.
benchmarks.analysis_method: WMDP-Chem accuracy; Grok 4.7 high (84.9%). Dual-use chemistry MCQ capability signal. Sources: model card PDF.

benchmarks.name: WMDP-Cyber
benchmarks.description: Cybersecurity subset of WMDP (Weapons of Mass Destruction Proxy). Multiple-choice questions measuring dual-use cyber knowledge relevant to enabling malicious actors to engage in offensive cyber operations.
benchmarks.analysis_method: WMDP-Cyber accuracy; Grok 4.7 high (88.1%). Dual-use cyber MCQ capability signal. Sources: model card PDF.
